Here at Scout Motors, we're carrying forward the heritage of one of the most iconic American vehicles in history. A vehicle dating back to 1960. One that forged the path for future generations of rugged SUVs and trucks and will do so once again.

But Scout is more than just a brand, it’s a legacy steeped in a culture of exploration, caretaking, and hard work.

The Scout brand is all about respect. Respect for the past and the future by taking an iconic American brand that hasn’t been around for a while, electrifying it, digitizing it, and loading it with American innovation. Respect for communities by creating a company that stands for its people and its customers. Respect for both work and play, with vehicles that are equally at home at a camp site, a job site, or on a Tuesday commute. And respect for our customers by developing two powertrains that meet their requirements — an all-electric powertrain as well as the Harvester™ range extender powertrain which includes a built-in gas-powered generator with an estimated 500 miles of combined range.

At Scout Motors, we empower our talented, inclusive, and entrepreneurial teams to innovate. What makes a Scout employee? Someone who is a visionary and a leader, who seeks new paths and shares lessons learned. A knowledgeable doer who collaborates across the company to build better. A go-getter with unrivaled passion.

The candidate must be articulate and possess strong technical troubleshooting abilities. The candidate demonstrates ownership and information retention abilities. The candidate possesses the ability to work independently, quickly and effectively to solve technical problems with hardware/software. In addition, the candidate provides an exemplary “white glove” level of customer service to internal clients.

  • Manages escalated tickets
  • Maintain and support A/V in conference rooms

jobs.title: Lifecycle Marketing Manager
jobs.description_text:
About The Weather Company:

The Weather Company is the world’s leading weather provider, helping people and businesses make more informed decisions and take action in the face of weather. Together with advanced technology and AI, The Weather Company’s high-volume weather data, insights, advertising, and media solutions across the open web help people, businesses, and brands around the world prepare for and harness the power of weather in a scalable, privacy-forward way. The world’s most accurate forecaster globally, the company reaches hundreds of enterprise clients and more than 360 million monthly active users via its digital properties from The Weather Channel (weather.com) and Weather Underground (wunderground.com).

AI is part of how we work:

Human judgment, expertise, and creativity remain essential and are amplified by AI. We expect everyone in this role to use AI thoughtfully and proactively to accelerate their performance, improve the quality of their work, and explore new possibilities. We are looking for people who are curious, adaptable, and excited to help shape an AI-enabled culture that delivers better outcomes for our customers and our company.

Job brief:

As a Lifecycle Marketing Manager at The Weather Company, you will own the moments that matter most to our users, from the first time they open the app to the habits that keep them coming back. Weather shapes daily decisions

jobs.title: Seasonal Customer Experience Associate
jobs.description_text:
We're passionate about customer experience here at Tecovas, and we're looking for Seasonal Customer Experience Associates to ensure our current and future customers have the best possible interaction with our brand and product. You will be on the forefront of our customer experience function and will have a role in shaping the strategy of a rapidly-growing brand. 

In order to provide our customers with the best holiday shopping experience, you will be required to be flexible with scheduling and available to work during the following:

  • Extended holiday hours that may include early morning shifts, weekends, and evenings.
  • Key holiday events, including:
    • The week of Thanksgiving (including the Friday after Thanksgiving),
    • The week of Christmas (including the day after Christmas), and
    • The week between Christmas and New Year's (including New Year's Day) 
  • Mandatory training: Oct 12 - 16 & Oct 19 - 23, 9am - 1pm CT

This is a temporary role with an expected start date of Oct 12 - Jan 16. Opportunities to become a permanent Customer Experience Associate may become available after the season, pending individual performance and business needs.

This is a remote position available to candidates located within the United States.

jobs.title: Manager, International Content Merchandising
jobs.location_raw: Los Angeles, CA (Hybrid); New York City, NY (Hybrid); USA - Remote
jobs.description_text:
About the Role:

Tubi is looking for an experienced content leader to lead editorial merchandising for Canada, Latin America, the United Kingdom, and Australia. This role blends creative curation with analytical rigor and operational excellence. You’ll drive merchandising strategies that surface the right content to the right audience, drawing from a deep understanding of regional preferences, strong data interpretation skills, and effective cross-functional execution.

Working closely with internal stakeholders and international sales and marketing teams, you'll own the content presentation strategy for four diverse catalogs—turning insights into programming action and campaigns that fuel engagement, viewership, and brand affinity.

Fluency in Spanish is a bonus, as is a deep appreciation for entertainment across genres and decades.

Location: LA/NY - hybrid in office Monday - Thursday. Ability to work in Eastern Time preferred.

What You'll Do:

  • Lead the merchandising and editorial strategy for four international markets: Canada, Latin America, the UK, and Australia.
  • Translate performance data and audience insights into actionable curation and merchandising decisions—across homepage programming, themed content containers, and tentpole campaigns.
  • Lead medium- and long-term planning cycles for international editorial priorities, coordinating closely with Programming, Product, Sale

jobs.title: Performance Partner
jobs.location_raw: San Francisco, CA; Los Angeles, CA; New York, NY (Hybrid)
jobs.description_text:
About the Role:

Tubi is creating a Performance Partner role to focus on supporting managers end-to-end in developing and managing their teams. This role will own the end-to-end Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) process, partner closely with HRBPs to develop and execute strategic talent programs, and drive manager effectiveness across the organization. This is a highly visible role that sits at the intersection of performance management, talent strategy, and manager enablement — ideal for someone who wants to build and own a program from the ground up.

This is an individual contributor role reporting to our VP of People. This role will be hybrid and can be based in SF/NYC/LA/Toronto.

What You'll Do:

  • Own the end-to-end Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) process — from initial documentation through execution, check-ins, and resolution — partnering with legal, managers and business leaders throughout
  • Partner with HRBPs on HR programs for their teams (e.g., performance reviews, onboarding, promotions), bringing performance management expertise into broader talent initiatives
  • Develop and execute strategic talent programs that drive manager effectiveness, bringing workforce trends and analytics into program design
  • Advise managers on trade-offs when navigating complex, undefined performance issues; encourage experimentation and iteration in how managers approach team development

About the Role:

Tubi is seeking a strategic and agile Sr. HRBP (Tech) to help us build a world-class People team responsible for providing high-quality support to employees, in close partnership with functions such as Talent Management, Total Rewards, Talent Acquisition, and Workplace. The Sr. HRBP (Tech) will act as a strategic thought partner to leaders across our Engineering and Product organizations, and tackle org issues with people-focused solutions aligned with business goals. This role will be responsible for empowering a culture of high performance, retaining and engaging talent, and driving velocity through simplicity across the tech team.

This role is critical to scaling a high-growth organization and driving operational efficiency across the People Team. You'll have a direct impact on the employee experience at Tubi — come bring your bright ideas to the team! 

This is an individual contributor role reporting to our VP of People. This role will be hybrid, based in SF.

What You'll Do:

  • Collaborate with tech management to support initiatives by understanding organizational objectives, issues, needs, and key success factors
  • Provide strategic business partnership and coaching to all levels of leadership
  • Design and drive talent programs to shape and reinforce our cultural values and mission

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Creator Marketing
jobs.description_text:
About the Role:

Tubi is looking for a Senior Manager, Creator Marketing to lead marketing strategy and execution for our growing slate of exclusive Creator titles.

This role will own the go-to-market approach for Creator exclusives, partnering across Content, Creator, Marketing, Growth, Social, PR and other teams to build campaigns that effectively bring a creator's fans to Tubi and introduce creators to new viewers among Tubi’s 110 million monthly active users. 

This role will help us understand what actually works—developing learning agendas, evaluating performance, designing experiments and translating those insights into stronger marketing strategies across the portfolio.

The ideal candidate is equal parts strategic marketer, analytical thinker and builder. They know how to turn a title into a compelling audience proposition, understand the unique role creators can play in driving discovery and fandom, and are energized by creating new playbooks rather than simply applying old ones.

This is a hybrid role based out of our Los Angeles office. You must be willing to travel to our Los Angeles office 2-3 days/week.

The Associate, Campaign Management supports the executional engine of the ad campaign lifecycle, working alongside the Revenue Operations team to keep sold campaigns running accurately and on schedule. jobs.title: Art Director, Opinion

The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination.
